newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania right stresses currency, privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania right stresses currency, privatisation.

text.p: Lithuania's system of regulating its currency, the litas, as well as privatisation, are two of the main themes the right-wing Homeland Union is pushing as it aims to lead the country's next government.
Lithuanians will vote on October 20 in a first round of the election and a second ballot will take place on November 10.

The Homeland Union, led by independent leader Vytautas Landsbergis and former prime minister Gediminas Vagnorius, hopes to become the largest party after the vote, unseating the former Communists of the Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party (LDLP).
The LDLP promises stability and more of the same slow, but it says steady, privatisation.
"Our main accent is on changing the financial and monetary policy to stimulate the economic process," Vagnorius, Homeland Union chairman, told Reuters in a recent interview.
Lithuania has a currency board system to maintain the litas at four to one dollar and the central bank has to match the amount of currency in circulation with hard currency reserves.
The central bank also lacks power to influence the litas with market intervention or interest rate movements.
But the Homeland Union has attacked the system, saying it has led to an overvalued litas, which strangles exports.
He said independent research had shown that the currency board system was harmful to the economy.
"I do not see why we should artificially destroy the national economy," he said.
Under an agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the currency board has to stay until October 1997.
But the IMF and Western diplomats believe the system is the only to keep inflation falling and trust in the litas.
One diplomat said Lithuanians themselves do not trust the currency and that Vagnorious would face a lot of problems if he attempts to get rid of the currency board.
"If he tried to implement this policy, he would get his fingers badly burned," the diplomat said. "They would see a run on the litas."
But one of the areas where Vagnorius has words to please the West is in privatisation.
The LDLP has been criticised for failing to attract foreign investment by not offering big state-owned companies for sale.
Vagnorius said his party would sell Lithuanian Airlines, the telecommunications company and the Mazheikiai oil refinery.
"We will sell in the privatisation programme all remaining objects such as energy, transport and communications companies with the exception of oil pipelines and electricity lines," Vagnorius added.
The party's manifesto says its privatisation programme would aim at being transparent and that sales of state companies would be by public offers, auctions and open tender.
